This entirely depends on where you're buying from and what your nutritional needs are. I've worked in a deli that sold "generic brand" meats with sodium in the thousands of milligrams per serving (2oz) along side Boar's Head, which has about 300mg of sodium per serving (again, 2oz). So obviously if sodium count was an issue for you, the choice there would be clear. Additionally, my husband has celiac disease so we generally avoid generic or store brand deli meats because they often contain gluten as a filler. I don't necessarily think all fillers are evil or bad for you, but just be aware of what's in the specific meat you're buying. If your deli can't supply you with a nutrition label for the meat, I wouldn't buy from them.
I believe "fresh" deli meat may be an oxymoron. ;)

There are few things that are really bad for you when eaten in moderation, a balanced diet is always the key. If you are eating nothing but deli meat then you are going to have a bad time, but if you're eating it as part of a balanced diet that includes fruits, vegetables and grains then you're probably going to be all right. Portion control is also, obviously, a thing.

Subway is pretty awful because of all the crap they put in their 'bread', but the concept of Subway is actually a really good one. A six inch, sourdough sub, as opposed to a Six Inch Sub(tm), with a couple of pieces of sliced deli meat and cheese and a big load of salad veggies is a really good lunch and combined with a low GI breakfast, and a good dinner with multiple servers of different colored, seasonal vegetables and a small piece of meat forms a part of a really good balanced diet. Combine this with regular exercise and you've got a pretty great recipe for health without any of the hyperbole and bullshit of low carb macrobiotic paleolithic lemon cleanses.

If you're looking for deli meats that are good for you look into making your sandwiches with a meat called "head cheese" it's high in proteins and good fats.
